name: sdns-automatic-recovery-of-failed-dns-listeners
instr:
Keep configured DNS endpoints available by automatically recreating failed listeners under an operator-controlled, bounded recovery policy. Recovery must preserve each transport's protocol behavior and resource ownership while making shutdown authoritative. Operators must be able to inspect recovery and request retries through the existing authenticated API.

A valid policy serializes attempts per endpoint, assigns monotonically increasing epochs, records exactly one terminal outcome per attempt, stops at the configured bound, and suppresses pending work after cancellation; disabled recovery preserves existing behavior without replacement attempts. Validation through `RecoveryConfig.Validate() error` in `github.com/semihalev/sdns/config` accepts disabled and finite policies, rejects negative `MaxAttempts` or `Delay` while identifying the setting, and performs no network work. Every replacement for UDP, TCP, TLS, DoH, DoH3, and DoQ either serves a valid request for its protocol or releases all resources acquired for that epoch before reporting failure or cancellation. Shutdown prevents new connections and serving epochs, releases configured addresses, and cannot resurrect certificates, watchers, packet connections, QUIC state, HTTP logging streams, or protocol servers. Exhausting UDP or TCP recovery coordinates server shutdown, while exhaustion of an optional listener remains observable without interrupting healthy listeners.
